system: Social Sciences: Communication and Interpersonal Skills
outline: Social Sciences: Communication and Interpersonal Skills
Auxiliary aids and alternative accessible formats
diagnosis: Effective communication accommodation for a patient with a vision disability
mechanism: Federal disability-rights requirements call for communication with patients with vision disabilities to be as effective as communication with others. When necessary, covered health programs should provide appropriate auxiliary aids or services such as qualified readers, Braille, large print, or accessible electronic formats, with the choice guided by effective communication and the individual's needs.
vignette: A 63-year-old woman with severe visual impairment is being counseled about a new long-term medication. She independently manages her health decisions but cannot read the standard-print medication instructions. She asks for the information in an electronic format compatible with her screen reader.
lead: Which response by the clinic is most appropriate?
correct: Provide the instructions in an accessible electronic format that permits effective communication
distractors: Require a family member to read the standard-print instructions to her
Provide the standard-print instructions because the same document is given to all patients
Ask her to sign a waiver stating that written instructions cannot be provided
Withhold written information and rely only on a brief verbal summary
distractor_notes: A support person does not remove the covered entity's responsibility to ensure effective communication when an auxiliary aid or accessible format is needed.
Providing identical inaccessible material does not make communication equally effective for a patient with a vision disability.
The appropriate response is to furnish an effective auxiliary aid or accessible format rather than shift the accessibility burden to the patient.
The nature and complexity of the communication matter; an accessible format can provide the same information independently rather than unnecessarily limiting the patient to a shortened summary.
key_expl: HHS disability-rights rules require covered health programs to take appropriate steps to ensure communication with people with vision disabilities is as effective as communication with others. Auxiliary aids and services can include Braille, large print, qualified readers, and accessible electronic information usable with a screen reader.
objective: Apply disability-access principles by selecting an effective accessible format for a patient with visual impairment rather than relying on family members, inaccessible standard print, waivers, or reduced information.

primary_competency: Medical Knowledge: Applying Foundational Science Concepts
diagnosis: Familial glucocorticoid deficiency caused by impaired ACTH receptor signaling
mechanism: MC2R encodes the adrenal ACTH receptor. Loss-of-function MC2R variants can prevent receptor trafficking to the cell membrane or ACTH binding, eliminating the ACTH signal that normally stimulates adrenal glucocorticoid production and causing childhood hypoglycemia and hyperpigmentation.
vignette: A 3-year-old boy has recurrent episodes of fasting hypoglycemia and progressive diffuse hyperpigmentation. He has no history of exogenous glucocorticoid use. Genetic testing identifies a biallelic loss-of-function variant in MC2R.
lead: The protein encoded by the mutated gene normally binds which hormone?
distractor_notes: MC2R encodes the ACTH receptor in the adrenal cortex, not the angiotensin II receptor involved in mineralocorticoid regulation.
TSH signals through the TSH receptor on thyroid follicular cells, whereas MC2R is the adrenal ACTH receptor.
LH acts through its own gonadal receptor and is not the ligand for MC2R.
ADH acts primarily through vasopressin receptors and is not the ligand for MC2R.
key_expl: MC2R encodes the adrenocorticotropic hormone receptor. ACTH binding normally stimulates adrenal glucocorticoid production; pathogenic MC2R variants can impair receptor trafficking or ACTH binding and cause familial glucocorticoid deficiency.
objective: Connect familial glucocorticoid deficiency due to MC2R loss of function with impaired adrenal ACTH-receptor signaling.

system: Behavioral Health, Nervous Systems and Special Senses
outline: Behavioral Health, Nervous Systems and Special Senses
NOTCH3 and vascular smooth muscle-cell degeneration
primary_competency: Patient Care: Diagnosis, including history and physical examination
diagnosis: CADASIL (cerebral autosomal dominant arteriopathy with subcortical infarcts and leukoencephalopathy)
mechanism: Pathogenic NOTCH3 variants impair Notch3 receptor function in vascular smooth muscle cells. Progressive dysfunction and loss of these cells damages small cerebral vessels, leading to migraine with aura, recurrent subcortical infarcts, white-matter disease, and eventual cognitive or mood changes.
vignette: A 42-year-old woman has recurrent migraines with visual aura and two prior lacunar strokes despite normal blood pressure, normal lipid levels, and no diabetes. Brain MRI shows extensive white-matter abnormalities. Her father and paternal aunt had strokes before age 50.
lead: Which diagnosis best explains this patient's findings?
distractor_notes: Multiple sclerosis is an inflammatory demyelinating disease and does not explain the autosomal-dominant pattern of premature small-vessel strokes with migraine and leukoencephalopathy.
MELAS is a mitochondrial disorder with a different inheritance pattern and multisystem phenotype; this pedigree and small-vessel arteriopathy pattern instead support CADASIL.
Antiphospholipid syndrome can cause arterial or venous thrombosis but does not produce a dominantly inherited NOTCH3-type small-vessel arteriopathy with characteristic white-matter disease.
Cerebral amyloid angiopathy is primarily an age-associated cerebral vessel disorder and is not the best fit for multiple early-adult subcortical strokes across successive generations.
key_expl: CADASIL is an autosomal dominant cerebral small-vessel disease caused by NOTCH3 variants. Vascular smooth muscle-cell dysfunction and death lead to migraines, recurrent strokes, leukoencephalopathy, and progressive neurologic impairment, often without conventional vascular risk factors.
objective: Recognize CADASIL from migraine with aura, recurrent premature subcortical strokes, white-matter disease, and an autosomal-dominant family history.

primary_competency: Patient Care: Diagnosis, including history and physical examination
diagnosis: Autosomal dominant tubulointerstitial kidney disease due to UMOD (ADTKD-UMOD)
mechanism: Pathogenic UMOD variants can prevent renal tubular cells from releasing uromodulin, causing intracellular protein accumulation and progressive tubulointerstitial injury. Reduced uric-acid excretion commonly causes hyperuricemia and early gout before progressive chronic kidney failure.
vignette: A 29-year-old man has recurrent gout and slowly progressive chronic kidney disease. Urinalysis shows no hematuria and only minimal protein. His father developed gout in his twenties and required kidney transplantation at age 48. Renal imaging shows no large cystic kidneys.
lead: Which inherited disorder best explains this presentation?
correct: Autosomal dominant tubulointerstitial kidney disease due to a UMOD variant
distractor_notes: Autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease is characterized by progressive renal cyst formation rather than the hyperuricemia/gout-predominant UMOD tubulointerstitial phenotype.
Alport syndrome is a hereditary basement-membrane disorder classically associated with hematuria and extrarenal hearing/ocular findings rather than early gout with a bland urine sediment.
Autosomal recessive polycystic kidney disease generally presents much earlier in life and is characterized by cystic renal disease rather than this dominantly inherited gout-CKD pattern.
Fabry disease is an X-linked lysosomal storage disorder with a different systemic phenotype and does not best explain this autosomal-dominant gout with progressive tubulointerstitial kidney disease.
key_expl: ADTKD-UMOD is an autosomal dominant kidney disease caused by UMOD variants. Mutant uromodulin can accumulate in renal cells, and affected patients often develop hyperuricemia and gout in adolescence or early adulthood followed by progressive kidney dysfunction.
objective: Recognize ADTKD-UMOD from early gout, progressive bland-sediment kidney disease, and autosomal-dominant inheritance, and connect it to abnormal uromodulin handling.

outline: ALPL deficiency and inorganic pyrophosphate accumulation
primary_competency: Medical Knowledge: Applying Foundational Science Concepts
mechanism: ALPL encodes tissue-nonspecific alkaline phosphatase, an enzyme essential for skeletal and dental mineralization. Reduced enzyme activity permits inorganic pyrophosphate to accumulate; pyrophosphate inhibits mineral deposition, producing poorly mineralized bones and teeth.
vignette: A 7-year-old girl has recurrent low-trauma fractures, bone pain, and premature loss of primary teeth. Serum calcium and phosphate concentrations are within reference ranges, but serum alkaline phosphatase activity is persistently very low.
lead: Accumulation of which substance most directly contributes to the defective mineralization in this disorder?
distractor_notes: Homogentisic acid accumulates in alkaptonuria and is not the substrate whose buildup impairs mineralization in ALPL deficiency.
Glucocerebroside accumulates in Gaucher disease rather than hypophosphatasia.
Cystine accumulates in cystinosis; the defining biochemical defect here is reduced tissue-nonspecific alkaline phosphatase activity.
Methylmalonic acid accumulates in methylmalonic acidemia or vitamin B12-related metabolic dysfunction, not as the direct inhibitor of bone mineralization in hypophosphatasia.
key_expl: Hypophosphatasia is caused by ALPL variants that reduce tissue-nonspecific alkaline phosphatase activity. The resulting accumulation of inorganic pyrophosphate inhibits mineralization of bone and teeth, explaining fractures, dental abnormalities, and low serum alkaline phosphatase.
objective: Connect low alkaline phosphatase with hypophosphatasia and identify inorganic pyrophosphate accumulation as the proximate inhibitor of skeletal and dental mineralization.
